runs.note: A speculative-decoding A/B on a DGX Spark (NVIDIA GB10, Linux) with native 0.1.62: llama.cpp v0.9.0 on CUDA. Qwen 3.8 27B Q4 ran with no speculation, MTP and DFlash2; Gemma 4 12B Q4 with none and MTP; Muse Glimmer 30B Q4 with none and DFlash2. Rows marked default use the catalog’s own setting and carry the plain model id. 903 trials, three per arm and scenario, ran November 13–22, 2026, in three rounds with the arm order rotated. Every trial’s engine log confirmed its speculation mode, and none was repeated, replaced or set aside. Speculation changed no measured quality: artifact review means match within 0.1, and no pass-rate difference is significant (Muse with DFlash2 +6.2 points, exact p = 0.055, one of ten tests). Eight failures came from time-based stops that faster decoding might have avoided: 4 for Qwen and 3 for Muse without speculation, 1 for Muse with DFlash2. They count as failures here. Task speeds are engine-log medians over every attempt; speculation decoded 2.7–2.9 times faster. Memory is not shown: the GB10 shares its memory with the GPU in a way the measurement cannot see. Artifact reviews are by Claude Sonnet 5.5, one column per rubric.
